key_insight: For D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr on DSS 2205, increasing spray distance to 190 mm produced the densest coating and the best corrosion resistance in acidic media.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance is a practical lever to improve coating compactness, reduce porosity, and extend service life of stainless-steel components exposed to aggressive acids.
method: D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm.
Evaluated corrosion in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization.
Compared coating morphology and porosity with SEM analysis.
evidence_signal: The 190 mm coating had the lowest reported corrosion rate (0.113 mmpy), versus 2.60 mmpy for the uncoated substrate, and porosity decreased from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm.
watch_item: The optimum distance is specific to the tested powder, substrate, and acid environment, so transfer to other systems may require re-optimization.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
